A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the revised title and expanded scope. Their main text, figures, equations, and complete proof appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix moves.

before.justification: V1 Figure 1 reports original synthetic multiclass experiments measuring losses, margins, and classifier correlations for NGD, SignGD, and Adam.

after.justification: V2 Section 8 and Figures 1–3 report original synthetic experiments, including Adam stability-constant effects and spectral/nuclear descent results.

M1.justification: V2 extends the optimization procedures studied to Schatten-norm NSD, introducing SVD-based spectral updates UV^T and rank-one nuclear updates uv^T (Section 3, Equation 6). V1 considered entry-wise norm NSD and Adam. The existing Adam/SignGD updates and linear cross-entropy model remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic Gaussian, linearly separable multiclass classification using cross-entropy. The changed sample counts and additional class-count configuration remain within this coverage; they change experimental settings rather than introduce a different task or domain.

E2.justification: The main loss/margin comparison retains NGD, SignGD, and the same four Adam stability-constant variants. However, v1 Figure 1(d,e) includes NGD and SignGD in the correlation comparison, whereas v2 Figure 2(d,e) restricts those panels to Adam variants.

E3.justification: The main experiment changes from 5 to 50 examples per class, and Adam trajectories extend to 10^5 iterations rather than approximately 10^4. V2 adds gradient-norm measurements and a spectral/nuclear experiment with 10 classes and 10 examples per class. Figure 1 also specifies stopping SignGD at 10^4 iterations because of numerical instability.

E4.justification: The existing stability-constant sensitivity check becomes a dedicated late-training analysis in v2 Figure 2. Gradient thresholds, margin trajectories, and classifier correlations investigate when nonzero stability constants change Adam's behavior, substantially extending v1's short-horizon observation of nearly overlapping curves.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 retains trajectory plots without adding uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 reports late transitions toward 2-norm behavior for nonzero-epsilon Adam, replacing v1's near-invariance finding, and adds spectral/nuclear margin and correlation results. Figure 1's dataset maximum margins change from 2.18/18.69 to 2.11/17.83 for the 2-norm/max-norm. These accompany changed experimental settings, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 6 and new Appendix E add Schatten-norm definitions, norm-ordering and Hessian bounds, and Theorem 6.2's unified margin-convergence result. V1's entry-wise NSD proofs move to Appendix D, while existing SignGD/Adam results largely remain. The added Lemma E.2 also contains a norm-square mismatch between its statement and Equation 31 in its proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden the central result to Schatten-norm NSD, including spectral and nuclear margin maximization. The introduction also replaces the claim of consistent behavior with small Adam stability constants with a two-phase empirical claim distinguishing zero and nonzero constants.

C2.justification: V2 explains Adam's transition through gradient/second-moment magnitudes becoming small relative to epsilon, relates it to Wang et al. (2021a), and qualifies the practical applicability of max-norm behavior. It also documents SignGD's numerical instability. The existing limitation to linear models and separable data remains.

D1.justification: V2 supplies learning-rate decay settings for the added spectral/nuclear methods and explicitly documents SignGD's stopping iteration and numerical reason. These are limited additions to experimental documentation; no release of this work's code or data is added.

R1.justification: V2 positions the Schatten-norm analysis as a first implicit-bias study and connects it to spectral descent, Shampoo, and Muon through new references. It also substantially refines the distinction from Wang–Scott and Ravi et al., emphasizing preservation of matrix geometry and the challenges of normalized updates.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, contributions become a numbered list, and the narrative gains dedicated NSD and Experiments sections. The entry-wise NSD and Adam appendices are reordered, and the proof overview moves from Appendix B to C. These reorganize the paper beyond simply adding results.

P2.justification: V1's single five-panel figure is reorganized into v2's four-panel main comparison and a separate five-panel Adam diagnostic figure. V2 also adds a four-panel spectral/nuclear figure, with new gradient plots, threshold lines, legends, captions, and extended iteration axes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the accuracy of the Adam discussion by replacing v1's broadly stated small-epsilon consistency with longer-training evidence and a qualified two-phase interpretation. The Schatten-norm extension adds a meaningful matrix-geometric result supported by derivations and experiments. Lemma E.2 introduces a local missing-square inconsistency, although its proof and Section 6 supply the squared bound; this defect does not outweigh the substantial theoretical and interpretive gains.
